original_test_intent: Validate four HIB PCIe-expander/switch thermal channels, TEMP_HIB_PEX1 through TEMP_HIB_PEX4, against the approved HIB/PEX specification across complete IB/OOB SDR, Sensor List and BMC Web evidence.
original_method: The HIB/PCIe owner maps each exact sensor to a physical PEX ASIC, board coordinate, stable device identity and sensing source, defines link/load-qualified thermal limits, and automation performs passive collection without touching PCIe state.
manual_activity: The HIB/PCIe/thermal owner resolves four exact HIB PEX identities and sensing points, approves device/topology and link-load-specific limits, and confirms the LP-labelled DeepSeek output is excluded before issuing a verdict.
required_inputs: Exact TEMP_HIB_PEX1 through TEMP_HIB_PEX4 names and populated count
HIB board revision, PEX ASIC model/instance and physical coordinate per index
Stable PEX identity such as PCI BDF plus device/serial/fabric identifier and port role
Sensing source definition: ASIC junction, internal diode, remote diode or HIB board probe
Units, scale, tolerance, refresh, unavailable/stale semantics and thresholds
Approved ranges by link width/speed, traffic/load, airflow and ambient condition
SDR entity/name/description plus Sensor List/Web mapping and same-target revisions
Secret-safe collectors and independent PCIe/thermal/BMC recovery
safety_requirements: Bind exact row 1891 and exclude row 1892 LP-chip evidence despite the shared code
Reject DeepSeek ai_logs_output naming TEMP_LP1~8_Chip as wrong-target evidence
Resolve four exact PEX members rather than query a literal tilde token
Correlate each reading with stable PEX identity and passive link/load state
Do not rescan PCIe, reload drivers, generate traffic, change cooling/thresholds/BMC or clear logs
Stop on missing device/sensor, topology change, stale/invalid value, link fault or thermal event
agent_execution_scope: Verify row/variant, source conflict, duplicate isolation and four-name expansion
Verify HIB/PEX topology, stable device identities and same-target mapping read-only
Collect complete IB/OOB SDR and Sensor List, four exact results and BMC Web
Compare identity/value/state/freshness with passive PCIe link/error/load/airflow/SEL context
Perform no LP substitution, PCIe action, workload, driver reload, mutation, retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve four-index HIB/PEX physical and stable-device map
Define junction/diode/board sensing semantics and link/load-qualified limits
Disposition the wrong TEMP_LP1~8_Chip DeepSeek output as non-acceptance evidence
Review all four PEX channels and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.command_recommendation: Resolve four exact HIB PEX names and stable ASIC identities, then collect complete secret-safe IB/OOB SDR/Sensor List plus Web and passive PCIe/link/thermal context; never accept LP output.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES HIB PEX IDENTITY PACKAGE AND WRONG-VARIANT OUTPUT QUARANTINE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a four-row mapping from exact sensor to HIB coordinate, PEX ASIC/BDF/device identity, sensing source and operating envelope, then reconcile complete views under the observed link/load state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Corrects the cross-variant output contract and makes PCIe ASIC identity and sensing point explicit before thermal comparison.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The following row's eight LP-chip results provide zero coverage for HIB PEX1–PEX4 even though the code is shared and DeepSeek copied that name.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: PEX numbering may follow board layout rather than PCI enumeration, and a remote board probe can lag junction temperature; wrong identity or sensor semantics can hide a switch thermal fault.

project_override_considerations: If a PEX instance is unpopulated or inaccessible, its expected absence must be owner-approved. BDF alone is insufficient if enumeration can change; bind an additional hardware/fabric identity.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, both same-code rows and documented DeepSeek output conflict
Approved four-name HIB coordinate/PEX ASIC/BDF/device/sensor-source map
Units, scale, freshness and link/load/airflow-qualified thermal criteria
Complete redacted IB/OOB SDR and Sensor List plus four exact results
BMC Web, same-target proof and passive PCIe link/error/load/SEL/ambient context
Explicit absence of LP1-LP8 substitution, statuses and output hashes

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Row 1891 Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target TEMP_HIB_PEX1~4, while its DeepSeek ai_logs_output names TEMP_LP1~8_Chip from same-code row 1892. The HIB review remains identifiable only by quarantining that wrong-variant output contract.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The original HIB PEX purpose and read-only method are clear; exact topology and limits are obtainable project inputs, so the DeepSeek mismatch does not create an irreducible blocker.

review_improvement: Records the cross-variant contamination as a source conflict, isolates LP evidence, and adds stable PEX ASIC identity plus sensing-source and link/load context.
independent_technical_reasoning: PCIe switch temperature can come from an internal junction sensor or a remote HIB probe, and PEX numbering need not track dynamic BDF order. The adjacent LP-chip name in the output field is therefore not a harmless label typo: accepting it would validate different devices and entirely miss the four target ASICs.
